title: Domain 4 extra questions (4.6-4.9)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks.

questions.stem: An employee transferred from Accounting to Marketing a year ago. An access review shows the employee can still open the accounting share and approve invoices in the finance system. Which of the following BEST describes this issue?
questions.explanation: Permission creep is the gradual buildup of access when old rights are not removed after a job change. Privilege escalation is an attack in which someone gains higher rights than they were granted, which did not happen here.

questions.stem: A new payroll analyst starts on Monday, and the identity team must create the account. Which of the following is the BEST way to provision the analyst's access?
choices: Grant only the access defined for the payroll analyst role
Copy the permissions of the analyst being replaced
Add the analyst to every group in the finance department
Grant broad department access and remove unused rights after 90 days
questions.answer: Grant only the access defined for the payroll analyst role
questions.explanation: Provisioning from a defined role gives the user only what the job needs, which follows least privilege. Copying another person's permissions is tempting but carries over any extra access that person accumulated.

questions.stem: A contractor's engagement ended three months ago, but the contractor's VPN account was still active and was used in a recent intrusion. Which of the following processes MOST likely failed?
questions.explanation: De-provisioning removes or disables accounts when a person leaves, and skipping it left a working account behind. Identity proofing verifies who someone is before an account is created, so it is not the step that failed here.

questions.stem: A help desk application needs to look up employees' phone numbers, managers, and group memberships stored in the company's central directory. Which of the following protocols would the application MOST likely use?
questions.explanation: LDAP is the standard protocol for querying and updating entries in a directory service. SAML exchanges authentication assertions between an identity provider and a service provider and is not used to browse directory attributes.

questions.stem: Employees use 12 internal web applications, each with its own username and password, and password reset calls are overwhelming the help desk. Which of the following would BEST reduce the number of credentials users must manage?
questions.explanation: Single sign-on lets users authenticate once with one set of credentials and reach all connected applications. Multifactor authentication strengthens each sign-in but adds a factor rather than reducing the number of credentials.

questions.stem: After an acquisition, the two companies use identity providers from different vendors. Architects require that both systems support common standards so each can trust the other's sign-in assertions. Which of the following concepts is the PRIMARY concern?
questions.explanation: Interoperability is the ability of different identity systems to work together through shared standards such as SAML. Attestation is a periodic review that confirms access is still needed, which does not address how two systems exchange trust.

questions.stem: A hospital creates a Billing Clerk group that holds every permission billing staff need. New clerks are added to the group and automatically receive those permissions. Which of the following access control models is in use?
questions.explanation: Role-based access control assigns permissions to a job function, and users inherit them through membership. Rule-based access control applies administrator-defined rules, such as time or source address limits, to everyone regardless of role.

questions.stem: A router's access list, written by the network administrator, is processed from top to bottom and permits or denies each connection based on source and destination, no matter which user is sending the traffic. Which of the following access control models does this describe?
questions.explanation: Rule-based access control evaluates a set of administrator-defined rules that apply to all traffic or users equally. Role-based access control depends on the user's job function, which the access list never considers.

questions.stem: Help desk technicians need to reset user passwords but should not be able to change anything else in the directory. Which of the following is the BEST way to grant this access?
choices: Add the technicians to the domain administrators group
Share one administrator account among the technicians
Give the technicians local administrator rights on every server in the domain
Delegate only the password reset permission to the help desk group
questions.answer: Delegate only the password reset permission to the help desk group
questions.explanation: Delegating only the needed permission follows the principle of least privilege. Adding technicians to the domain administrators group would work but grants far more rights than the task requires.

questions.stem: A company wants a sign-in method that resists phishing. Employees will plug a small USB device into their laptops, and the device will prove possession of a private key to the website without the user typing any code. Which of the following is the company deploying?
questions.explanation: Security keys use public key cryptography bound to the website's address, so a fake site cannot capture a usable secret. Soft and hard tokens display one-time codes that a user can be tricked into typing into a phishing page.

questions.stem: During testing, a fingerprint reader grants access to a person who is not enrolled in the system. Which of the following biometric measurements describes this error?
questions.explanation: The false acceptance rate measures how often a biometric system wrongly accepts an unauthorized person. The false rejection rate is the opposite error, in which a legitimate user is denied.

questions.stem: A bank's sign-in system blocks access when a user's connection comes from a country where the bank has no customers, even when the password is correct. Which of the following authentication factors is being evaluated?
questions.explanation: Location derived from the source network or GPS is the somewhere-you-are factor. Something you are refers to biometrics such as a fingerprint or face, which the system is not checking.

questions.stem: Field technicians who do not carry company smartphones receive a small key fob with a screen that shows a new six-digit code every minute for remote sign-in. Which of the following BEST describes this device?
questions.explanation: A hard token is a dedicated physical device that generates one-time codes. A soft token produces the same kind of code but runs as an app on a phone or computer.

questions.stem: Because each business application requires a different complex password, many employees write their passwords on sticky notes. Which of the following would BEST let employees keep unique, strong passwords without writing them down?
questions.explanation: A password manager stores unique, strong passwords in an encrypted vault so users only remember one master secret. Allowing reuse reduces the burden but means one stolen password unlocks many systems.

questions.stem: Employees now sign in to their laptops with face recognition that unlocks a cryptographic key stored in the device, and they never type a password. Which of the following BEST describes this approach?
questions.explanation: Passwordless authentication replaces the password with factors such as biometrics and device-bound keys. Single sign-on reduces the number of sign-ins but still typically relies on a password for the first one.

questions.stem: A security team wants to make user passwords harder to crack by brute force. Which of the following changes would be MOST effective?
choices: Require a password change every 30 days
Require at least one special character
Remember the previous 24 passwords to prevent reuse
Raise the minimum length from 8 to 16 characters
questions.answer: Raise the minimum length from 8 to 16 characters
questions.explanation: Each added character multiplies the number of possible passwords, so length gives the greatest gain against brute force. A single required special character adds far less, because users place it in predictable positions.

questions.stem: Attackers use usernames and passwords stolen from a breached shopping website to sign in successfully to several employees' corporate email accounts. Which of the following password practices MOST likely enabled this?
questions.explanation: The employees used the same password on a personal site and at work, so credentials stolen elsewhere worked at the company. Password expiration forces periodic changes but would not stop reuse of the current password across sites.

questions.stem: Administrators no longer know the root passwords for critical servers. They check a password out of a secure repository, every use is logged, and the password is changed automatically after it is checked back in. Which of the following is being used?
questions.explanation: Password vaulting stores privileged credentials in a protected repository with checkout, logging, and rotation. Just-in-time permissions grant elevated rights for a limited time, but they do not involve checking out a stored shared password.

questions.stem: A deployment job receives cloud access keys that are generated for that job alone and expire automatically after 15 minutes. Which of the following BEST describes these keys?
questions.explanation: Ephemeral credentials are short-lived and created for a single session or task, so a stolen key quickly becomes useless. Static service account keys stay valid until someone rotates them, which is the risk ephemeral credentials avoid.

questions.stem: An audit finds that 40 employees hold permanent domain administrator rights and that shared admin passwords are stored in a spreadsheet. Which of the following would BEST address both findings?
choices: A stronger password complexity and history policy
questions.explanation: A privileged access management solution vaults admin credentials and grants elevated rights only when needed, addressing both the standing rights and the spreadsheet. A data loss prevention system watches for sensitive data leaving the company and does not control admin access.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY security benefit of just-in-time permissions for administrators?
choices: Elevated rights exist only for the short time they are needed
Administrators never need to authenticate again
Shared admin accounts can be used by more people
Audit logging of administrator activity is no longer required at all
questions.answer: Elevated rights exist only for the short time they are needed
questions.explanation: Just-in-time permissions remove standing privileges, so there is little or no elevated access for an attacker to steal at any given moment. They do not remove authentication or logging; those remain essential controls.

questions.stem: A developer requests a test environment through a portal, and automation builds the virtual machines from an approved hardened image, places them on the correct network, and applies required tags. Which of the following automation use cases does this describe?
questions.explanation: Resource provisioning automatically creates infrastructure such as servers and networks to a standard. User provisioning creates accounts and access for people, not the systems themselves.

questions.stem: When HR marks an employee as terminated, a workflow immediately turns off the person's accounts in every application and revokes the VPN certificate. Which of the following automation use cases is this?
questions.explanation: Automatically disabling access when a person leaves removes rights quickly and consistently across systems. Resource provisioning builds infrastructure and has nothing to do with removing a departing user's access.

questions.stem: A vendor announces a critical flaw in the Telnet service on its network devices. Within minutes, a script turns off Telnet on every affected switch in the company. Which of the following automation use cases is this?
questions.explanation: Automation that turns services on or off across many systems at once reduces exposure quickly. User provisioning manages people's accounts and would not change which services run on a switch.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY security benefit of automating account de-provisioning?
choices: New hires receive accounts before their first day of work
Former employees lose access promptly and consistently
Users can choose their own group memberships
Account activity logs no longer need review
questions.answer: Former employees lose access promptly and consistently
questions.explanation: Automated de-provisioning removes access the moment a departure is recorded, closing the window in which an old account can be misused. Creating accounts before a start date is a provisioning benefit, not a de-provisioning one.

questions.stem: Automation places each new cloud server into the correct virtual firewall rule set based on its tag, so web servers accept only HTTPS and database servers accept traffic only from the web tier. Which of the following automation use cases is this?
questions.explanation: Security groups act as virtual firewalls for cloud resources, and automation can assign and maintain them consistently. User provisioning deals with people's accounts, not network rules for servers.

questions.stem: The deployment pipeline automatically rejects any infrastructure template that would allow SSH from the entire internet, regardless of who submits it. Which of the following BEST describes this control?
questions.explanation: Guard rails are automated limits that stop people from making changes that break policy, even when they otherwise have permission. Resource provisioning builds the infrastructure but does not by itself block an unsafe design.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes a guard rail in security automation?
choices: A script that pages a manager when a ticket goes unanswered too long
A pipeline step that compiles and packages source code
An automated check that blocks actions that violate policy
A screen that summarizes current alert counts
questions.answer: An automated check that blocks actions that violate policy
questions.explanation: A guard rail keeps users inside safe boundaries by automatically preventing noncompliant actions. Paging a manager about an unanswered ticket is escalation, a different automation use case.

questions.stem: In a cloud environment, which of the following acts as a virtual firewall that automation can attach to instances to control their inbound and outbound traffic?
questions.explanation: A security group is a set of allow rules applied to cloud instances, functioning as a virtual firewall. A playbook is a documented or automated response procedure and does not filter traffic.

questions.stem: Whenever the intrusion detection system raises a high-severity alert, the orchestration platform automatically opens a record in the IT service management system with the alert details and assigns it to the SOC queue. Which of the following automation use cases is this?
questions.explanation: Automatically opening a tracked work item for each alert is ticket creation. Escalation would raise the priority or notify higher-level staff, which is not described here.

questions.stem: A playbook raises an incident to critical severity and notifies the CISO when ransomware indicators appear on more than ten hosts. Which of the following automation use cases does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Escalation automatically moves an issue to higher priority or more senior responders when conditions are met. Ticket creation only records the issue and does not notify leadership based on its growing impact.

questions.stem: Hardware monitoring detects that a server's disk is failing, and automation opens a work order for the data center team with the server name and error details already filled in. Which of the following automation use cases is this?
questions.explanation: Automatically generating a work order from a monitored event is ticket creation, which ensures the problem is tracked to resolution. Nothing here raises priority or notifies senior staff, so it is not escalation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST likely reason a SOC automates ticket creation from SIEM alerts?
choices: To avoid the need to investigate alerts
To ensure every alert is recorded and tracked to closure
To delete duplicate and low-value log entries from the SIEM database
To let users approve their own access requests
questions.answer: To ensure every alert is recorded and tracked to closure
questions.explanation: Automatic tickets give each alert an owner and an audit trail so nothing is lost. Creating a ticket does not replace investigation; analysts still have to work the ticket.

questions.stem: A SOC wants its orchestration platform to pull reputation data from a threat intelligence service and push block rules to firewalls from two different vendors. Which of the following makes this possible?
questions.explanation: APIs let different products exchange data and commands, which is how integrations between security tools are built. Guard rails restrict what changes are allowed but do not connect systems to each other.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY security benefit of continuous integration and testing?
choices: Production servers no longer need patching
Developers no longer need code reviews
Flaws are found early, as each code change is merged
Applications can skip user acceptance testing before release
questions.answer: Flaws are found early, as each code change is merged
questions.explanation: Running automated builds and security tests on every merge catches problems while they are small and cheap to fix. It does not remove the need for patching, reviews, or acceptance testing.

questions.stem: A response script isolates infected hosts by calling the EDR vendor's API, and the API key is stored in plaintext inside the script. Which of the following is the BEST way to reduce the risk?
choices: Rename the script so its purpose is less obvious to attackers
Email the key to the team for safekeeping
Retrieve the key from a secrets vault at run time
questions.answer: Retrieve the key from a secrets vault at run time
questions.explanation: A secrets vault keeps the key encrypted and controls who and what can read it, so the key is not exposed in code. Renaming the script is obscurity only; anyone who opens it still sees the key.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes continuous integration?
choices: Code is released only once a year after a long manual review by the team
Code is merged often, and each merge is built and tested automatically
A change board approves every infrastructure change
Developers test code only on their own laptops
questions.answer: Code is merged often, and each merge is built and tested automatically
questions.explanation: Continuous integration means frequent merges into a shared repository, each automatically built and tested. An annual manual release is the opposite approach and lets problems pile up between releases.

questions.stem: Before automation, analysts took about 40 minutes to block a malicious IP address after an alert. Now a playbook blocks it within seconds. Which of the following benefits of automation does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: The key change is how fast the organization responds, which is reaction time. Workforce multiplier is about a small team handling more work, which is not what this scenario measures.

questions.stem: SOC analysts were leaving because of repetitive alert triage. After the company automated those tasks, analysts spent more time on investigations, and turnover dropped. Which of the following benefits of automation does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Removing tedious work improves job satisfaction and helps keep skilled staff, which is employee retention. Reaction time is about how quickly threats are handled, not whether staff stay.

questions.stem: During seasonal demand, an online retailer's web servers grow from 20 to 300 within hours, and each new server receives the same security controls without manual work. Which of the following benefits of automation does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Automation lets the environment grow quickly while every new system is still built securely. A workforce multiplier describes staff productivity, while this scenario is about growing infrastructure safely.

questions.stem: Every branch office router is now deployed from the same automated template, so all routers have identical, approved settings from the first day. Which of the following benefits of automation does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Building every device from one template produces consistent, standard configurations and avoids one-off mistakes. Reaction time concerns the speed of response to events, not how devices are built.

questions.stem: A monthly user access report used to take an analyst two days to compile by hand. A script now produces it in ten minutes. Which of the following benefits of automation does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Turning two days of manual work into minutes is efficiency and time saving. Reaction time refers to how quickly the organization responds to a security event, and a monthly report is not a response.

questions.stem: Before buying an orchestration platform, a manager warns that linking 15 tools with branching playbooks will be hard to design, understand, and troubleshoot. Which of the following considerations is the manager raising?
questions.explanation: The concern is how intricate the automation will be to build and maintain, which is complexity. Technical debt comes from shortcuts taken over time, and nothing has been built yet.

questions.stem: A proposed SOAR project would require new licenses, paid integration services, and training for every analyst, and the total is well above the security budget. Which of the following considerations does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Licenses, services, and training are all expenses, so the concern is cost. Complexity is about how hard the automation is to design and run, not how much it costs.

questions.stem: Before approving a new automation project, the CIO asks who will maintain the scripts, update them when vendor APIs change, and fix them when they break over the coming years. Which of the following considerations is the CIO raising?
questions.explanation: Ongoing supportability is whether the organization can keep automation working over time as systems change. A single point of failure is one component whose loss stops everything, which is not what the CIO is asking about.

questions.stem: A company's orchestration server runs every automated response playbook. Which of the following would BEST reduce the risk that a failure of this server stops all automated responses?
choices: Write additional playbooks for the platform
Deploy the platform as a high-availability cluster
Grant more administrators access to the platform's console
questions.answer: Deploy the platform as a high-availability cluster
questions.explanation: A high-availability cluster removes the single point of failure by keeping the service running if one node fails. Adding more playbooks only puts more work on the same failing server.

questions.stem: A SIEM alert flags unusual outbound traffic from a file server. An analyst reviews related logs to confirm whether it is a real incident and to determine which systems are involved. Which of the following phases of incident response is this?
questions.explanation: Analysis confirms that an incident is real and works out its scope and impact. Detection is the point at which the alert is first raised, which has already happened.

questions.stem: After the malware has been removed, the team rebuilds the affected servers from clean backups, verifies them, and monitors them closely before returning them to production. Which of the following phases of incident response is this?
questions.explanation: Recovery restores systems to normal operation and confirms they are working and clean. Eradication is the earlier step of removing the malware itself.

questions.stem: An attacker is using a compromised employee account to browse sensitive file shares right now. Which of the following actions would BEST contain the incident?
choices: Reimage every workstation in the company
questions.explanation: Disabling the account immediately cuts off the attacker's access, which is the goal of containment. Reimaging every workstation is disruptive, slow, and does not stop an attacker who is using valid credentials.

questions.stem: Without warning the SOC, an internal red team runs a realistic attack against test systems while responders detect and handle it with their normal tools. Which of the following BEST describes this activity?
questions.explanation: A simulation tests people and tools against a realistic, hands-on scenario. A tabletop exercise is a discussion of how the team would respond, with no systems involved.

questions.stem: After an incident, a review finds that help desk staff did not know they had to notify the SOC when users reported suspicious pop-ups. Which of the following would BEST prevent this in the future?
choices: A full simulation exercise for the executive leadership team
Incident response training for help desk staff
A threat hunt by the SOC
questions.answer: Incident response training for help desk staff
questions.explanation: Training makes sure staff know their role in the response process, including when and how to escalate. A simulation for executives would not teach the help desk its reporting duties.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY advantage of a tabletop exercise compared with a full simulation?
choices: It tests tools under realistic attack conditions
It tests plans and roles at low cost with no risk to systems
It measures exactly how fast production systems can be restored
It requires no planning or facilitator
questions.answer: It tests plans and roles at low cost with no risk to systems
questions.explanation: A tabletop is a guided discussion, so it is inexpensive and cannot disrupt production. Testing tools under realistic attack conditions is the strength of a simulation, not a tabletop.

questions.stem: A tabletop exercise reveals that no one knows who is authorized to take the payment system offline during an incident. Which of the following should the organization do NEXT?
choices: Repeat the same exercise next week without changes
Remove the payment system from the scope of future exercises
Update the incident response plan to assign that authority
questions.answer: Update the incident response plan to assign that authority
questions.explanation: Exercises exist to find gaps, and the gap is fixed by updating the plan and the roles it defines. Repeating the exercise without changes would expose the same problem again.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY purpose of root cause analysis after an incident?
choices: To identify which employee caused the incident so they can be disciplined
To restore affected systems to production
To find the underlying cause so the incident does not recur
questions.answer: To find the underlying cause so the incident does not recur
questions.explanation: Root cause analysis looks past the symptoms to the condition that allowed the incident, so it can be corrected. Restoring systems is the recovery phase and does not explain why the incident happened.

questions.stem: A public web server has been reimaged twice after malware infections, and each time it is reinfected within a week. Which of the following should the team perform to stop this from happening again?
questions.explanation: Repeated reinfection means the entry point was never found, and root cause analysis is how the team finds and fixes it. A tabletop exercise tests the response plan but does not investigate this specific weakness.

questions.stem: A root cause analysis finds that ransomware entered through a server that allowed Remote Desktop connections directly from the internet without MFA. Which of the following is the BEST corrective action?
choices: Replace every workstation in the office
Block internet access to Remote Desktop and require MFA
Add the ransomware sample's hash to the antivirus blocklist
questions.answer: Block internet access to Remote Desktop and require MFA
questions.explanation: Fixing the exposed service and requiring MFA addresses the root cause that let the attacker in. More frequent backups speed recovery but leave the same door open.

questions.stem: A customer database went offline because its TLS certificate expired, and the team renewed the certificate. The manager says this only treated the symptom. Which of the following BEST addresses the root cause?
choices: Restart the database server every week
Disable TLS on the database connection
Automate certificate expiration monitoring and renewal
Document the outage in the help desk ticket and close it
questions.answer: Automate certificate expiration monitoring and renewal
questions.explanation: The real cause was the lack of a process to track and renew certificates, so automating that prevents a repeat. Weekly restarts do nothing about expiring certificates.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes threat hunting?
choices: Investigating each alert after the SIEM correlates and raises it
Searching proactively for threats that evaded existing defenses
Reviewing firewall rules for unused entries
questions.answer: Searching proactively for threats that evaded existing defenses
questions.explanation: Threat hunting assumes an attacker may already be present and looks for evidence without waiting for an alert. Responding to SIEM alerts is reactive monitoring, the opposite of a proactive hunt.

questions.stem: A threat hunter wants to build a hypothesis about which attacker techniques are most likely to be used against the company. Which of the following sources would BEST support this?
choices: Help desk statistics on the number of password resets each month
Threat intelligence on groups targeting the company's industry
questions.answer: Threat intelligence on groups targeting the company's industry
questions.explanation: Intelligence about the tactics used by attackers who target similar organizations gives hunters realistic hypotheses to test. Password reset statistics describe help desk workload, not attacker behavior.

questions.stem: During a hunt, an analyst finds a workstation contacting an unfamiliar domain every 60 seconds, although no alert has fired. Which of the following should the analyst do NEXT?
choices: Close the hunt because no alert fired
Wait to see whether the SIEM eventually raises an alert
Delete the related logs to save space
Escalate the finding to the incident response team
questions.answer: Escalate the finding to the incident response team
questions.explanation: Regular beaconing is a strong sign of command-and-control, so it should enter the incident response process. Waiting for the SIEM ignores the very gap the hunt just exposed.

questions.stem: Which of the following outcomes of a threat hunt MOST improves the organization's future detection?
choices: New detection rules based on what the hunt found
Fewer data sources fed into the SIEM
questions.answer: New detection rules based on what the hunt found
questions.explanation: Turning hunt findings into new detections means the same activity raises an alert next time. Shortening log retention removes the data hunters and detections depend on.

questions.stem: Before examining a suspect's drive, an analyst connects it through a write blocker, makes a bit-by-bit copy, and then works only on the copy. Which of the following forensic activities is this?
questions.explanation: Acquisition is collecting evidence, such as a forensic image, in a way that does not change the original. A legal hold is an instruction to preserve data for litigation, not the technical copying of a drive.

questions.stem: Which of the following would BEST show that a forensic image has not been altered since it was collected?
choices: Storing the image on an encrypted drive in a locked safe
A signed statement from the analyst
Matching its hash to the hash recorded at acquisition
questions.answer: Matching its hash to the hash recorded at acquisition
questions.explanation: A matching hash proves the image is bit-for-bit identical to what was captured. Timestamps are easy to change and do not prove the contents are unchanged.

questions.stem: In a contract dispute, opposing counsel requests all emails and documents about the contract from the past three years. The company searches its systems, collects the matching files, and produces them. Which of the following does this describe?
questions.explanation: E-discovery is the process of finding, collecting, and producing electronically stored information for legal proceedings. A legal hold only requires that relevant data be kept and not deleted; it does not cover searching for and producing it.

questions.stem: After finishing an investigation, a forensic examiner writes a document describing the tools and methods used, the evidence examined, and the findings, for management and possible court use. Which of the following forensic activities is this?
questions.explanation: Reporting documents the process and conclusions so others can understand and rely on them. Preservation protects the evidence from change but does not explain what was found.

questions.stem: Responders photograph a seized laptop, seal its drive in a tamper-evident bag, and store it in a locked, climate-controlled evidence room so it stays in its original condition. Which of the following forensic concepts does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Preservation keeps evidence protected from alteration, damage, or loss. A legal hold is a directive from counsel to keep data for litigation, not the physical safeguarding of seized items.

questions.stem: Policy allows only the application server to connect to the database server. An analyst needs to see every allowed and denied connection to the database, including source address and port. Which of the following data sources would BEST provide this?
questions.explanation: Firewall logs record which connections were permitted or blocked, with addresses and ports. Application logs record what users did inside the application, not every network connection attempt.

questions.stem: An unknown device appeared on the office network. An analyst needs to know which switch port its MAC address first connected to and when. Which of the following data sources should the analyst review?
questions.explanation: Network logs from devices such as switches record link events and the MAC addresses learned on each port. A vulnerability scan might find the device but would not show where and when it plugged in.

questions.stem: A sensor receives a copy of network traffic from a SPAN port and generates alerts on attack signatures, but it cannot drop any packets. Which of the following BEST describes the logs this sensor produces?
questions.explanation: A passive sensor fed from a SPAN port is an intrusion detection system, so it alerts but cannot block. An IPS sits inline and can drop traffic, which this sensor cannot do.

questions.stem: An analyst suspects malware on a workstation is using randomly generated domain names to find its command server. Which of the following data sources would BEST show this behavior?
questions.explanation: DNS query logs show every name a host tried to resolve, so many random-looking names stand out. Firewall logs usually record IP addresses rather than the domain names a host looked up.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to see who logged in to a Linux server over SSH and which commands were run with sudo. Which of the following should the analyst review?
questions.explanation: The operating system's authentication log records SSH sign-ins and sudo use. The web server access log records HTTP requests to the website, not shell logins.

questions.stem: While investigating a server, an analyst finds a Windows event showing that the security log was cleared shortly after an unknown service was installed. Which of the following does this MOST likely indicate?
choices: An attacker attempting to hide activity
A failed cumulative operating system update
questions.answer: An attacker attempting to hide activity
questions.explanation: Clearing the security log right after an unexpected change is a classic sign of an attacker covering tracks. Normal log rotation archives or overwrites old entries automatically and is not recorded as a manual clear following a new service.

questions.stem: An investigator suspects an employee copied confidential files to a personal USB drive. Which of the following data sources would BEST confirm when the drive was connected and which files were copied?
choices: Endpoint logs from the employee's workstation
questions.answer: Endpoint logs from the employee's workstation
questions.explanation: Endpoint logs record device connections and file activity on the computer itself. Network-based sources such as firewall logs never see files copied to a local USB drive.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to see which pages a user requested on the company's online storefront and the HTTP status code returned for each request. Which of the following data sources would BEST provide this?
questions.explanation: Web server access logs record each requested URL along with its status code and client address. Firewall logs show the connection to the server but not which pages were requested inside it.

questions.stem: A customer relationship application log shows that the account jsmith exported 50,000 customer records at 2:00 a.m. The user normally exports about 100 records during business hours. Which of the following is MOST likely occurring?
choices: Data exfiltration using the user's account
questions.answer: Data exfiltration using the user's account
questions.explanation: An unusually large export at an odd hour from a valid account suggests the account is being used to steal data. A brute-force attack would appear as repeated failed sign-ins, not as a bulk export.

questions.stem: A web application log contains the entry `GET /products?id=1' UNION SELECT username,password FROM users-- HTTP/1.1 200`. Which of the following attacks does this show?
questions.explanation: The UNION SELECT statement inside the parameter is an attempt to make the database return extra data, which is SQL injection. Cross-site scripting injects script code into pages viewed by other users, not database queries.

questions.stem: A cloud email service's sign-in log shows successful logins for the same user from Chicago and from Singapore 20 minutes apart. Which of the following does this MOST likely indicate?
questions.explanation: No one can travel between those cities in 20 minutes, so this impossible travel suggests an attacker is signing in with stolen credentials. An account lockout would appear as denied sign-ins, but both of these succeeded.

questions.stem: A confidential document was posted online. Investigators examine the document's properties and find the author name and the name of the computer that created it. Which of the following data sources did the investigators use?
questions.explanation: File metadata stores details about a document, such as its author, creation time, and originating system. A packet capture records network traffic and would not exist for a file created long before.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes metadata in an investigation?
choices: The full contents of every network packet
Data that describes other data, such as sender and time
A list of missing patches on each server
A real-time display of current alert counts across all systems
questions.answer: Data that describes other data, such as sender and time
questions.explanation: Metadata is information about data, such as who created or sent it, when, and how large it is. The full contents of packets is a packet capture, which includes payloads rather than just descriptive details.

questions.stem: A user reports a suspicious email. The headers show that the Return-Path domain does not match the From domain, and the SPF check result is fail. Which of the following does this MOST likely indicate?
choices: The message was encrypted in transit
The message came from an internal server
questions.explanation: A failed SPF check means the sending server is not authorized for that domain, and the mismatched domains support spoofing. Encryption in transit is not reflected by SPF results or a domain mismatch.

questions.stem: Most traffic leaving the network is encrypted, so investigators cannot read the contents. Which of the following would still show source, destination, port, bytes transferred, and duration for each session?
questions.explanation: Flow records are metadata that summarize each conversation without its contents, so they remain useful when traffic is encrypted. Packet payloads of encrypted sessions cannot be read without the keys.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to reconstruct the exact file that a workstation downloaded over unencrypted HTTP an hour ago. Which of the following data sources would BEST support this?
questions.explanation: A packet capture holds the full contents of the traffic, so the file can be rebuilt from it. Flow records show that a transfer happened and how large it was, but not what was in it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common limitation of packet captures during an investigation?
choices: They record only the source and destination addresses of each session
They can be collected only from endpoints
They need large storage and cannot read encrypted data without keys
questions.answer: They need large storage and cannot read encrypted data without keys
questions.explanation: Full captures grow quickly, and encrypted payloads stay unreadable without the session keys. Recording only addresses describes flow data, which is a limitation captures do not have.

questions.stem: A security team suspects a legacy inventory application sends user passwords across the network in cleartext. Which of the following is the BEST way to confirm this?
choices: Review the antivirus logs on each user's workstation for alerts
Capture and inspect the application's network traffic
questions.answer: Capture and inspect the application's network traffic
questions.explanation: Inspecting captured packets shows exactly what the application sends, including any readable passwords. Firewall deny logs only list blocked connections and would never show the content of allowed traffic.

questions.stem: An IDS alert shows only a signature name and the two IP addresses involved. To decide whether the alert is a true positive, which of the following should the analyst review?
choices: The packets that triggered the alert
questions.answer: The packets that triggered the alert
questions.explanation: Looking at the actual packets lets the analyst see whether the traffic really contains the attack the signature describes. The firewall rule base shows what is allowed but not what was in this traffic.

questions.stem: The CISO wants one screen showing current counts of critical alerts, open incidents, and unpatched systems that updates continuously during an incident. Which of the following would BEST meet this need?
questions.explanation: A dashboard presents live, summarized data from many sources on one screen. A weekly report is periodic, so it cannot show the current state while an incident is unfolding.

questions.stem: Every Monday, the compliance team receives an emailed summary from the SIEM listing the previous week's failed logins and privileged account changes. Which of the following data sources is this?
questions.explanation: An automated report is generated on a schedule and delivered to its audience. A dashboard is viewed live on screen rather than sent as a periodic summary.

questions.stem: IDS logs show exploit attempts for a specific flaw against 30 servers. The analyst needs to know which of those servers are actually susceptible so they can be prioritized. Which of the following data sources would BEST help?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability scan results show which systems have the flaw, so the team can focus on servers the attacks could succeed against. Flow records confirm that traffic reached the servers but not whether they are vulnerable.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST appropriate use of automated reports in security operations?
choices: Watching an attack unfold in real time
Reconstructing files from captured network traffic
questions.explanation: Automated reports deliver the same summary on a schedule, which suits management review and audits. Watching an attack in real time is the job of a dashboard or live monitoring.
